context: This prompt requests adding visual indicators for prompt workflow flags in the Active Prompt page's buttons row. The flags track the prompt's lifecycle state (questionnaire generated/answered, plan generated, implementation completed, executed) and modification tracking (modifications count and current modification ID). These indicators will help users quickly understand the prompt's current workflow state without navigating through tabs or the registry.

questions.question-text: Where in the buttons row should the flag indicators be displayed?

options.label: In a new column to the right of the action buttons (New, Mod, Complete)
options.pros: Clear separation from action buttons, dedicated space for status indicators, won't interfere with button clicking
options.cons: Takes up more horizontal space, may require restructuring the row layout on smaller screens

options.label: Below the action buttons in a separate status bar within the same control panel
options.pros: Doesn't compete for horizontal space, clear visual hierarchy, easily expandable
options.cons: Takes up vertical space, pushes content down, may feel disconnected from the action buttons

options.label: To the left of the action buttons
options.pros: Status information appears first (left-to-right reading), keeps all indicators in one row
options.cons: May create visual clutter, could be overlooked as users focus on buttons first

options.label: Integrated within or adjacent to the execution mode selector (right column)
options.pros: Utilizes existing space, groups workflow state with execution mode
options.cons: May overcrowd the execution mode selector, could confuse the distinction between state and mode

questions.recommendation-rationale: Placing the indicators in a separate status bar below the buttons provides the clearest visual separation between actions (buttons) and state information (flags). This approach is more scalable, won't interfere with button interactions, and allows for consistent display across different screen sizes. The vertical space usage is minimal and acceptable for improving workflow visibility.

questions.question-text: What visual style should be used for the boolean flag indicators?

options.label: Bootstrap icons with color coding (green checkmark for true, gray X or empty icon for false)
options.pros: Consistent with Bootstrap UI, clear true/false distinction, visually intuitive, accessible
options.cons: May look cluttered with many icons in a row, requires careful color selection for accessibility

options.label: Small colored badges with abbreviated labels (e.g., 'Q-Gen', 'Q-Ans', 'Plan', 'Impl', 'Exec')
options.pros: Text labels provide clarity, badges are standard Bootstrap component, can use different colors per flag
options.cons: Takes more space, abbreviations may not be immediately clear to new users

options.label: Minimalist dots/circles with tooltips (solid dot for true, empty circle for false)
options.pros: Very compact, clean minimal design, tooltips provide full information on hover
options.cons: Requires hovering to understand meaning, less immediately accessible, may be too subtle

options.label: Icon-only badges that show only when true, with tooltips for explanation
options.pros: Minimal visual clutter, only shows relevant active states, clean appearance
options.cons: Doesn't show complete picture of workflow state, users can't see what flags are false

questions.recommendation-rationale: Bootstrap icons with color coding provide the best balance of clarity, accessibility, and visual design consistency. They offer immediate visual feedback without requiring hover interaction, are consistent with the existing RDD Web UI design patterns, and can be made accessible with proper ARIA labels. The true/false state distinction through color and icon choice (checkmark vs X or circle) is universally understood.

questions.question-text: How should the icon indicators be labeled to ensure users understand what each flag represents?

options.label: Short text labels next to each icon (e.g., 'Quest. Gen:', 'Quest. Ans:', 'Plan:', 'Impl:', 'Exec:')
options.pros: Immediately clear without hovering, self-documenting, accessible for screen readers
options.cons: Takes significant horizontal space, may become cluttered on smaller screens

options.label: Tooltips only (shown on hover), with icons in a consistent order
options.pros: Clean compact design, doesn't take extra space, users learn the order over time
options.cons: Not immediately clear to new users, requires hovering, less accessible

options.label: Very short abbreviations (1-2 letters) with tooltips for full names
options.pros: Compact but provides some context, tooltips available for clarity
options.cons: Abbreviations may be ambiguous (Q? QG? QA?), still requires memorization

options.label: Icon legend/key displayed once at the top, then just icons in the status bar
options.pros: Clean status bar, educational legend helps new users, minimal repetition
options.cons: Users must remember mapping, legend takes space, may be overlooked

questions.recommendation-rationale: Short text labels provide the best user experience for a workflow-critical interface. While they take more space, the clarity and accessibility benefits outweigh the cost. Users can quickly scan and understand the prompt state without prior knowledge or hovering. This is especially important for the RDD framework where understanding workflow state is essential for correct operation.

questions.question-text: How should the modifications-count and current-modification-id be displayed?

options.label: As separate inline text elements with labels (e.g., 'Mods: 5' and 'Current: M-003')
options.pros: Clear and explicit, easy to read, follows common UI patterns
options.cons: Takes horizontal space, may seem verbose for simple numeric values

options.label: As a single combined badge (e.g., 'Mods: 5/M-003' or 'Mods: 5 (M-003)')
options.pros: More compact, groups related information, cleaner visual appearance
options.cons: May be harder to parse, especially when current-modification-id is null

options.label: Only show when relevant (modifications-count only when > 0, current-modification-id only when not null)
options.pros: Minimal clutter, shows only actionable information, cleaner when no modifications exist
options.cons: Users may wonder if modifications feature exists if never shown, inconsistent display

options.label: As icon-based indicators (modification icon with count badge, and current mod highlighted differently)
options.pros: Visually consistent with other flags, compact icon-based design
options.cons: May be less clear for numeric information, requires hover for details

questions.recommendation-rationale: Showing modification information only when relevant reduces visual clutter and focuses user attention on actionable information. Most prompts won't have modifications initially, so always displaying 'Mods: 0' adds no value. When modifications exist, showing the count is helpful. When a modification is in progress, showing the current ID is critical. This conditional display aligns with the principle of progressive disclosure.

questions.question-text: What format should be used for displaying current-modification-id when it is not null?

options.label: Full modification ID format with leading zeros (e.g., 'Current: 001', 'Current: 023')
options.pros: Matches the modification file naming convention exactly, consistent with backend
options.cons: Leading zeros may be unnecessary for display purposes, slightly verbose

options.label: Simplified numeric format without leading zeros (e.g., 'Current: 1', 'Current: 23')
options.pros: Cleaner and more readable, users understand numeric values easily
options.cons: Slight inconsistency with modification file naming (modification-001.md)

options.label: Abbreviated format with 'M-' prefix (e.g., 'Current: M-1', 'Current: M-23')
options.pros: Clear indicator that it's a modification ID, balance between clarity and brevity
options.cons: Adds extra characters, M- prefix might be redundant in context

options.label: Icon indicator only with tooltip showing the full modification ID
options.pros: Most compact visual design, full information available on demand
options.cons: Requires hover interaction, less immediately visible

questions.recommendation-rationale: The simplified numeric format provides the best readability without unnecessary visual noise. Since the context already indicates it's a modification ID (through label or position), the numeric value alone is sufficient. Leading zeros serve a purpose for file sorting but don't add value in UI display. This approach is cleaner and more user-friendly while still being clear.
